declared.title: Inappropriate causal assumptions underlie Killingsworth, Kahneman, and Mellers’ conclusions
declared.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
declared.foundIn: counter-evidence report reports/money-happiness/counter-evidence.md; OpenAlex search « Inappropriate causal assumptions underlie Killingsworth Kahneman Mellers » (2026-11-22)

population: methodological letter on the quantile regressions of Killingsworth 2023 (no new data)

findings.text: A quantile regression describes a percentile of a distribution, not a group of people such as « the least happy 15% »

support.sentence: What quantile regression does not do is simply estimate regressions in particular subgroups of people—such as the 15% least happy.
support.readBy: dossier agent (money-happiness), PMC11572929 full text (BioC), paragraph 6

findings.text: With no covariates, the 2023 reanalysis cannot rule out confounding: its « increases » are associations

support.sentence: Given that KKM do not take into account any covariates, assuming the absence of confounding is not warranted.
support.readBy: dossier agent (money-happiness), PMC11572929 full text (BioC), paragraph 4

limits: a methodological letter: it says how to read the 2023 result, not whether money helps
the authors of the 2023 paper reply that they never claimed a precisely invariant group (Killingsworth 2024)
